headline: The Verge says Nvidia's new RTX Spark laptops, which use Arm chips, are meant to run all Windows apps and games, though early tests show limits and high prices.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a major chip maker enters Arm-based Windows laptops; verdict is early and partly opinion.
importance_line: It could widen choice beyond Intel, AMD and Apple chips for laptop buyers, but the machines cost $2,600 to $5,900 and some games run slowly.
summary: The Verge reports, in an early hands-on opinion piece, that Nvidia's first RTX Spark laptops, which run full Windows 11 on an Arm-based chip, go on sale on 16 October, with Nvidia saying they will run all apps and games, including those with strict anti-cheat software. The Verge's testers found most games run smoothly but some processor-heavy ones stay near 30 frames per second, and the machines cost $2,600 to $5,900 partly because memory prices have surged.
notes: Opinion plus early testing; Nvidia statements are company claims.
